passage: Ayesha, come here. I'm Elizabeth. I was ten when my father lost his job. He sat us down and said, "My work has stopped. I will look for another one. We are okay, and we will not lose our home right now." I went quiet. Then I asked, "Will I still get my school shoes?" He laughed a bit, and said, "Yes, you will." After that I went outside and played gilli-danda till dark, as if nothing was different. That night I woke up and cried and could not say why. My mother sat by the bed and held my hand. I was glad they told me plainly. Not knowing would have been worse.

qa.q: How old was Elizabeth when Elizabeth's father lost his job?
What was Elizabeth feeling that night when waking and crying?
qa.a: A delayed sadness and fear that had not shown during the day, though Elizabeth could not say why.

qa.q: What did Elizabeth's father do that reassured Elizabeth?
qa.a: He told the children plainly that his work had stopped, that he would look for another job, and that the family was okay for now.

qa.q: How might Elizabeth's mother have seen Elizabeth's reaction that night?
qa.a: With care. The mother sat by the bed and held Elizabeth's hand without needing an explanation for the tears.

grounding: A child told about the father's job loss goes quiet, asks an odd question, keeps playing, and cries later; a plain honest explanation helps.

passage: The rain was heavy and the school bus was due in ten minutes. Noor knelt by Joseph's chair. "Joseph, I have sad news. Bruno died in the night. He was old and he wasn't in pain." Joseph looked at the cereal bowl. "Will he be cold?" Noor swallowed. "No, sweetheart. He is not feeling cold or anything now." Joseph nodded, finished the cereal, put on the raincoat, and asked, "Can I take my umbrella with the duck?" Noor stared, then said, "Of course." At bedtime that night, Joseph crept into the room and said, "I miss Bruno." Noor held Joseph close, and they cried together.

qa.q: What did Joseph ask Noor after hearing the news?
What was Joseph feeling when asking for the umbrella with the duck?
qa.a: Probably taking the news in slowly, carrying on with everyday things while the sadness had not yet arrived.

qa.q: What did Noor do that helped Joseph?
qa.a: Noor told the news simply and honestly, answered the odd question calmly, and later held Joseph close at bedtime.

qa.q: How might Noor have felt seeing Joseph ask about the umbrella?
qa.a: Surprised and perhaps unsure, but Noor stayed calm and said "Of course," accepting that children react in different ways.

grounding: A child told a pet has died goes quiet, asks odd questions and carries on, with the sadness arriving later, even under a time constraint.
